answer: The primary purpose of thoracentesis is therapeutic: to remove accumulated pleural fluid that is compromising ventilation and reducing intrathoracic pressure on the lungs. The additional diagnostic value is that the aspirated fluid can be submitted for analysis (cell count, cytology, chemistry, culture) to help identify the underlying cause of the effusion (e.g., transudate versus exudate, infectious versus neoplastic etiology), guiding further management.
